claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To get started, could you please tell me how many children you're looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I'd like to find out if I can claim Child Benefit. I have one child - Alex, who is 8 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! It's great to meet you, and I'm happy to help assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

I have a few more questions to help determine your eligibility:

Are you responsible for Alex's care? For example, do they live with you, or do you pay towards their upbringing?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives with me and I'm responsible for his care.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that. That's helpful to know.

Next question: Is Alex a British citizen, or do they have the right to live in the UK? And are you yourself living in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, that's the thing - I don't actually live in the UK at the moment. We're living abroad.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know. That's an important detail.

Could you tell me a bit more about your situation? Specifically:

Are you (or your spouse/partner, if applicable) working abroad for the UK government, or are you employed by a UK-based organisation that has sent you overseas? Or are you living abroad for other reasons?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, we're not working for the UK government or anything like that. We're just living abroad for personal reasons - it's not a work posting or anything official like that.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. I have one more question to be thorough:

Are you or your spouse/partner a Crown servant (such as a diplomat or member of the armed forces posted overseas), or do you work for a company that is registered in the UK and pays National Insurance contributions for you?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nothing like that. We're not Crown servants or diplomats, and I'm not working for a UK company that's paying National Insurance for me. We're just living abroad as regular residents here.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for providing all that information. Based on what you've told me, I now have enough details to make an assessment of your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, I'm afraid **you are not currently eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's why:

**For Alex (age 8):** To claim Child Benefit, you generally need to be living in the UK. While there are some exceptions for people living abroad—such as Crown servants (diplomats, armed forces), those working for the UK government overseas, or people employed by UK-based companies that pay UK National Insurance contributions—you've confirmed that none of these apply to your situation.

Since you're living abroad for personal reasons and don't fall into any of the exempted categories, you unfortunately don't meet the residency requirements for Child Benefit.

**What you could do:**
- If your circumstances change and you return to live in the UK, you would likely become eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex at that point (as long as Alex is still under 16, or under 20 and in approved education or training).
- If your work situation changes and you begin working for a UK employer who pays National Insurance contributions for you, this could also affect your eligibility.

I hope this helps clarify things. Is there anything else you'd like to know?
